Soundcore Liberty 5 earbuds hit a record low at 42% off

Anker's Liberty 5 noise canceling earbuds drop to $75.99, with LDAC, Dolby Audio, and multipoint support.

•

Nov 26, 2026 — 11:39 AM ET

•

•

SoundGuys

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Anker’s Soundcore Liberty 5 pack a lot of features for midrange earbuds, and they just hit their lowest price. They’re down to $75.99 on Amazon, which is $54 off the $129.99 list price and a new record low. Every color is on sale at the same price.

Noise canceling is the headline feature. The Soundcore Liberty 5 use Adaptive ANC 3.0, which keeps recalibrating as your surroundings change, so they keep up whether you’re on a bus, in a coffee shop, or walking past traffic.

Sound quality gets plenty of attention too. LDAC support means higher quality wireless audio from compatible Android phones, and Dolby Audio can be switched on in the Soundcore app for a wider, more spacious sound. Multipoint lets you connect to two devices at once, and it keeps working with LDAC turned on, which isn’t always the case.

Battery life is rated at up to 12 hours per charge with noise canceling off, or eight hours with it on, and the case extends that to as much as 48 hours. A 10-minute charge adds about five hours of listening. Six microphones handle calls, and an IP55 rating means sweat and rain aren’t a worry.

At $75.99, the Soundcore Liberty 5 are a great pick for Android users who want strong noise canceling and LDAC without paying flagship prices.

items.body: Apple's annual four-day Black Friday through Cyber Monday shopping event is now live in Australia , New Zealand , and Thailand , and it will continue to roll out across Europe, the U.S., and Canada as the calendar turns to Friday, November 27 around the world. In the U.S., Apple's terms and conditions say the promotion begins on November 27 at 12 a.m. Pacific Time and ends on November 30 at 11:59 p.m. Pacific Time. During the shopping event, customers can get an Apple gift card with the purchase of an eligible product at an Apple Store, in the Apple Store app, and on Apple.com. However, the gift card can only be used towards future purchases, and higher immediate discounts on Apple products are frequently available at Amazon and other resellers. In the U.S., Apple is offering gift cards worth up to $300 with the purchase of an eligible iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, HomePod, AirPods, Beats headphones, Beats Pill speaker, Apple Pencil Pro, and select Magic Keyboards for iPads. For the first time ever, Apple is also offering a $25 gift card with select third-party accessories from brands including Anker, Belkin, Mophie, Nimble, Rains, and Twelve South. The selection includes chargers and MacBook covers. As usual, many of Apple's newer products are excluded from the offer, including the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, iPhone Duo, MacBook Neo, latest models of the iPad mini, Apple TV 4K, iMac, and Mac Studio, and more. Refurbished products are also ineligible, and the offer cannot be combined with educational pricing. Halide Adds Fill Light Feature for iPhone Duo

Thursday November 26, 2026 8:17 am PST by Hartley Charlton

Halide 3.4 can use the iPhone Duo's outer display to light subjects when the device is unfolded. The feature offers softer lighting than the dedicated flash, with maximum screen brightness recommended. Users can also show subjects a camera preview on the outer display. The update adds a larger inner-screen viewfinder and brings back the shutter timer and color and luminance histograms on other iPhones.

Samsung’s Galaxy S26 FE has just hit its lowest price. The unlocked phone is down to $499.99 on Amazon, which is $200 off its $699.99 list price and the first time it has dropped below $500. Shoppers rate it 4.6 out of five stars on Amazon.

The Galaxy S26 FE sits just below Samsung’s flagship S26 series and borrows plenty from it. You get a large 6.7-inch display with a smooth 120Hz refresh rate, which keeps scrolling, gaming, and video looking fluid, along with 8GB of RAM for comfortable multitasking.

The 50MP main camera is backed by Samsung’s photo tools, including the AI Photo Editor and Photo Assist for quick fixes and creative edits, and Super Steady video helps keep footage smooth when you’re on the move.

Galaxy AI features come built in, and Samsung promises seven years of OS and security updates, so this is a phone you can comfortably keep for a long time. A 4,900mAh battery should get most people through a full day without hunting for a charger.

This is the 128GB model in Graphite, and it’s sold and shipped by Amazon.

At $499.99, the Samsung Galaxy S26 FE delivers most of the flagship experience for much less, and this is the cheapest it has been.

items.title: Exclusive: Samsung is working on a private cloud for Galaxy AI, and it could look a lot like Apple’s
items.summary: Code in One UI 9.5 Beta 1 reveals an unreleased "SPAC" framework to process anonymized cloud-based Galaxy AI requests.
items.body:
Affiliate links on Android Authority may earn us a commission. Learn more.

General technology

Exclusive: Samsung is working on a private cloud for Galaxy AI, and it could look a lot like Apple’s

Code in One UI 9.5 Beta 1 reveals an unreleased "SPAC" framework to process anonymized cloud-based Galaxy AI requests.

•

Nov 26, 2026 — 10:06 AM ET

•

•

Joe Maring / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• Code in One UI 9.5 Beta 1 points to “SPAC,” a new Samsung framework for processing AI requests on its servers while keeping them private.

• SPAC appears to closely follow Apple’s Private Cloud Compute blueprint, and the code references AI models like Google’s Gemma 4 and Alibaba’s Qwen 3.6.

• SPAC doesn’t seem to be active on the Galaxy S26 Ultra yet, and Samsung hasn’t announced it either.

Galaxy AI has always made you choose between privacy and capability. Features that run on your phone keep your data there. However, the more capable ones, like Writing assist, Note assist, and generative photo edits, send your data to Samsung’s servers. Samsung’s current promise for those is a policy one: Photo Editor, for instance, tells you your image “will be sent to servers for processing… but not stored by Samsung.” If you’d rather not take that on trust and face value, the only option is the “Process data only on device” toggle in Galaxy AI Settings, which switches those cloud-based features off entirely.

Apple pitched a way around that trade-off two years ago when it launched Private Cloud Compute with Apple Intelligence in iOS 18. Private Cloud Compute (PCC) promises to extend device-level privacy to server-side AI processing: your request still goes to a server, but it’s encrypted, anonymized, and processed in a way that even Apple says it can’t access. Google and Meta have since built their own versions, with Google promising your personal data stays private to you and is not accessible to anyone else, “not even Google.” Now, code in the One UI 9.5 beta suggests Samsung is building its own take on the idea, and it looks a lot like Apple’s.

APK teardown

This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship.

You're reading an Android Authority exclusive story you won’t find anywhere else. An APK teardown helps predict features that may arrive on a service in the future based on work-in-progress code. However, it is possible that such predicted features may not make it to a public release. More Authority Insights →

Samsung’s “SPAC” and “Arcane” are new in One UI 9.5

Digging through One UI 9.5 Beta 1 on our Galaxy S26 Ultra over the past week, we found a new Samsung SDK called “SPAC” inside four apps: Photo Editor, IntelliVoiceService (Samsung’s speech and language service), Smart Capture, and PhotoRemasterService. None of these apps had it in One UI 9.

Based on the code, SPAC seemingly connects to a server-side gateway that Samsung’s code calls “Arcane”, alongside separate token, identity, and fraud detection services.

While we looked around, we could not find what SPAC stands for. If we’re allowed to guess, it could refer to “Samsung Private AI Cloud,” but it could just as easily be called something else. (Yes, SPAC also stands for Special Purpose Acquisition Company, the shell companies used to take businesses public. We don’t know whether this is coincidental or intentional — probably the former rather than the latter.)

SPAC appears to be designed so your AI requests stay private

It’s early days, but it seems most of SPAC’s code deals with privacy and trust rather than AI. Based on the code, it appears to work in a few layers:

• A middleman for your requests: User requests appear to pass through a third-party relay first, so Samsung can see what you asked but not where it came from.

• Servers that have to prove themselves: Your phone appears to check that Samsung’s server is running genuine, untampered software before it sends anything.

• A public-style record: Samsung’s server software appears to be logged in a record that can’t be quietly changed, so it can’t swap in something different for some users.

• Anonymous passes: Your phone appears to get one-time passes that prove you’re a real Galaxy user without revealing which user you are.

The code also includes an “unattested” mode in which the phone skips some of these checks, but this could be for internal testing only.

SPAC seems to follow the blueprint Apple laid out for Private Cloud Compute

Apple

Apple explained how Private Cloud Compute works back in June 2024, and Samsung’s SPAC looks remarkably similar so far.

In Apple’s system, requests carry no identifying information. They’re approved with one-time passes that aren’t tied to you, and they go through a third-party relay that hides your IP address. Apple also logs its server software in a public record that can’t be quietly changed, and iPhones only send data to servers that match that record. SPAC’s code appears to have a match for almost every one of those pieces.

Apple

Apple isn’t the only one doing this. Google’s Private AI Compute, which launched in November 2025, also sends requests through third-party relays to hide where they came from, and uses anonymous passes to keep your identity separate from your AI requests. Meta’s Private Processing for WhatsApp’s AI features works much the same way, with outside companies running the relay and the public record.

So far, it doesn’t seem like Samsung is inventing anything new here. It appears to be adopting what has become the industry’s standard recipe for private cloud AI, spelled out first by Apple. If anything, Samsung is late to the party. Apple, Google, and Meta all announced their systems publicly and explained how they work. Samsung hasn’t said a word yet about its plans for a private cloud AI system for users, but SPAC might just be it.

SPAC’s code references Gemma 4, Qwen 3.6, and FLUX.2

SPAC code within the above-mentioned apps references open-weight AI models from Google and Alibaba, which Samsung could run on its own servers. We couldn’t confirm that Galaxy AI uses any of them right now on our Galaxy S26 Ultra.

Aamir Siddiqui / Android Authority

The above code snippet is from Smart Capture, which powers the AI select feature, and it shows the app relying on Alibaba’s Qwen 3.6 and Google’s Gemma 4 as options. IntelliVoiceService references Gemma 4, while PhotoRemasterService references Black Forest Labs’ FLUX.2 klein 4B and a Stable Diffusion model.

Aamir Siddiqui / Android Authority

Photo Editor also makes reference to OpenAI’s TTS models, Samsung’s own Gauss, and Meta’s V-JEPA, but doesn’t seem to be using them.

Aamir Siddiqui / Android Authority

Which Galaxy AI features could use SPAC?

Adamya Sharma / Android Authority

Based on the code, several Galaxy AI features could use SPAC. AI select could get smarter at understanding what’s on your screen, for instance, pulling several events from a screenshot into your calendar at once. Photo Editor’s cloud AI eraser and cloud photo upscaling, including zoomed camera shots, appear set to move to SPAC. So does live speech translation, through a route Samsung’s own code labels “private.”

The code also maps everyday Galaxy AI tasks like summarizing, tone changes, emoji suggestions, writing help, and Now Brief to SPAC, along with an unnamed “GUI agent” and something called “Bixby work.” If all of this moves over, a large part of Galaxy AI’s cloud features could eventually run through SPAC instead of Samsung’s current servers.

SPAC doesn’t seem to be live on the Galaxy S26 Ultra yet

On our S26 Ultra, SPAC appears to be switched off for now:

• Smart Capture and Photo Editor only use SPAC on a newer Galaxy AI version than our S26 Ultra reports, the same gate as Recompose.

• PhotoRemasterService needs a newer Remaster version than the S26 Ultra has.

• IntelliVoiceService only uses SPAC for translation when an app asks for a “private” cloud mode, and we could not trigger this yet.

We used Writing assist, AI select, Note assist, Now Brief, and Interpreter while logging the phone’s activity. None of them touched SPAC, and all of them used Samsung’s existing Galaxy AI cloud or ran on the device. There’s also no user-facing text about SPAC anywhere in the build, so there’s no new consent screen or privacy notice yet. So while code about SPAC does exist in One UI 9.5 Beta 1 for the Galaxy S26 Ultra, it doesn’t seem to work right now.

It’s also not yet clear how SPAC will work with the existing “Process data only on device” toggle in Galaxy AI Settings. We found Photo Editor checking the toggle, but not Smart Capture’s or IntelliVoiceService’s SPAC code, though Samsung could be handling it elsewhere in One UI.

Samsung’s servers, on the other hand, appear to be further along than the phone software. Public certificate records show production server addresses for SPAC that Samsung has kept renewing over the past few months, and newer entries suggest it’s adding servers in the US as well.

The back end for SPAC could already be in place, waiting for the features to switch on.

A private cloud could matter for Galaxy AI

Stephen Radochia / Android Authority

If SPAC works as the early code in this beta suggests, Samsung could swap today’s “not stored by Samsung” policy promise for one it can prove: running more powerful Galaxy AI features in the cloud while keeping your requests about as private as on-device processing.

Such a change would put Galaxy AI on equal footing with Apple Intelligence and Gemini on privacy. It could also matter more if Samsung starts charging for Galaxy AI Premium and leans harder on server-side models.

We’ve reached out to Samsung for more details on SPAC, and we’ll update this article when we hear back.

LG’s S6FTR soundbar kit just dropped to its lowest price. The complete 5.1-channel system is down to $219.99 on Amazon, which is $180 off its $399.99 list price and $30 below its previous low of $249.99.

The LG S6FTR comes with everything you need for surround sound in one box. Alongside the main soundbar, there’s a subwoofer for deeper bass and a pair of rear speakers to place behind your seating. The setup is a good fit for living rooms where a TV’s built-in speakers struggle with dialogue and bass, and it’s much simpler than piecing together a receiver and separate speakers.

items.body: Kodak licensee Reto this week introduced the SlideTag, a $34.99 Find My-compatible item tracker with a color E Ink screen for displaying personal photos. The SlideTag's design draws on Kodak's Kodachrome slide mounts, placing a square display inside a retro frame with an attachment point for a keyring. Its 1.54-inch screen has a resolution of 240 × 240 pixels and uses six ink colors to reproduce images. As it is an E Ink panel, it retains a static image without needing continuous power to display it. Users can manage photos through the Kodak Memory Link app for iOS and Android, separately from the accessory's tracking features. They can transfer up to 12 images over Bluetooth and arrange them into slideshows, or use the screen to display information such as contact details, a QR code, or a to-do list. Once paired with Apple's Find My app, the SlideTag can be located through the ‌Find My‌ network. There is also support for Google's Find Hub. A built-in buzzer provides an audible way to find nearby belongings. The device uses a replaceable CR2032 battery and has an IP54 rating for dust and splash resistance. Its plastic enclosure measures 39.3 × 46 × 7.58mm and weighs 16.6 grams, making it wider and taller than the current AirTag , but slightly thinner. Apple's tracker measures 31.9mm in diameter and 8mm thick, and weighs 11.8 grams. The ‌AirTag‌ also has a higher IP67 rating, providing protection against immersion in water up to one meter deep for up to 30 minutes. Apple takes its online store down for a few hours ahead of Black Friday every year to tease its annual gift card offer with the purchase of select products. The store is down in Australia , New Zealand , and Thailand , right now, and it will eventually go down in Europe, the United States, and Canada. In the U.S., Apple is offering gift cards worth up to $300 with the purchase of an eligible iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, HomePod, AirPods, Beats headphones, Beats Pill speaker, Apple Pencil Pro, and select other accessories. The offers will be available from November 27 through November 30 in participating countries. Many readers email us about Apple's online store going down ahead of Black Friday, so this is our annual reminder that it does not relate to new products . Black Friday is one of the few occasions per year when Apple directly offers deals on its products, but better deals are often available through resellers like Amazon, so make sure to check out our Black Friday deals coverage for the latest discounts. Speaking on the latest episode of the "Power On" podcast , Gurman revived discussion about the device, known internally as "Project J312." He described it as a foldable iPad with a display measuring around 19 to 20 inches, saying it would resemble a "gigantic iPhone Duo with no display on the outside." The device could cost between $3,000 and $5,000. Apple apparently originally wanted to announce the device by 2027, before pushing that target to 2028. The timeframe has since slipped to around 2029, although Gurman cautioned that it remains uncertain whether the product will ever reach the market. Gurman cited cost and display manufacturing yield issues among the obstacles facing development, along with concerns that the ‌iPad‌ could be cumbersome. Apple has also yet to determine which operating system it would run, with macOS, iPadOS, and an entirely new platform all remaining possibilities. Gurman described the unresolved software direction as another complication, but expressed excitement about the device's potential. The comments follow a report from research firm Omdia in September, which claimed that Apple had canceled plans for a foldable MacBook measuring between 16.1 and 18 inches when unfolded. Earlier reports had described that device as a large-screened foldable ‌iPad‌, although it remains unclear whether Omdia was referring to the same project Gurman discussed. Gurman discussed the foldable ‌iPad‌ in April, describing it as a priority for John Ternus while warning that it could remain an unreleased experiment. The potential 2029 timeframe was already part of Gurman's report from October 2025 , when weight and display technology issues were said to threaten Apple's earlier 2028 target. TL;DR

• Android Auto is working on a new Details page in settings that provides all the relevant information about a device and display.

• There’s also a button to copy all the vehicle and device information, which should make it easier to report bugs.

• We also found a relocated speedometer in Google Maps, plus a bunch of new manufacturer icons that could land in a future update.

Android Auto is no stranger to bugs, and a future version of the app could make it easier to submit your device/car information in bug reports. Google is working on an updated Connected vehicles page with a new option to instantly copy and share relevant details.

APK teardown

This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship.

You're reading an Android Authority exclusive story you won’t find anywhere else. An APK teardown helps predict features that may arrive on a service in the future based on work-in-progress code. However, it is possible that such predicted features may not make it to a public release. More Authority Insights →

We examined Android Auto version 18.3.164844 to enable a new Details option from the Android Auto settings page. This opens a “Vehicle information” dialog containing all the necessary information, including the car’s make and model, software version, display dimensions, and more.

As you would expect, the display details in the Vehicle information dialog are visible only when you’re connected to Android Auto. Meanwhile, there’s a Copy option here that lets you paste all these details into a bug report instantly.

When available, this new Details option should appear on the Connected vehicles page, accessible by tapping Vehicles in Android Auto settings, then tapping your car’s name. Currently, this page only contains the Forget and Rename options.

While we managed to uncover visuals of the new Details page in Android Auto settings, a string in the app’s code reveals another future addition.

Code

<string name="locked_app_not_supported_toast">This app is locked and cannot be opened in Android Auto</string>

Users will likely see the above toast when trying to open an Android Auto-compatible app that’s been locked via the upcoming app lock functionality. While app lock isn’t widely available on Android just yet, this string suggests Google is laying the groundwork for its future arrival.

Additionally, the Google Maps experience in Android Auto could get a minor tweak, with the speedometer icon moving from the bottom-left of the screen to the top-left. This opens up space in the bottom-left portion of the screen, which can sometimes be blocked by the speedometer.

Lastly, Android Auto is in the process of adding new OEM icons to the system. We’re seeing a handful of popular OEMs here, including some motorcycle brands.

The icon typically appears as the first option in the app drawer, as shown in the second screenshot above. Tapping this icon lets users exit the Android Auto experience instantly.

Since we had to manually activate some of these features, it’s hard to say when Android Auto will incorporate these changes. All we can do is hope that it happens sooner rather than later.

items.body:
iPhones Dominate China's Weak Singles' Day Smartphone Sales

Thursday November 26, 2026 4:55 am PST by Tim Hardwick

Apple held the top spot in China's smartphone market during the country's Singles' Day shopping festival, despite an 8% year-over-year sales decline, according to Counterpoint Research. The overall market fell 17% across the promotional period, defined as weeks 42–46.

Six of the top 10 bestsellers were iPhone 17 and 18 models, led by the iPhone 18 Pro Max, with the iPhone Duo at No. 9. Huawei was the only major brand to grow in the period, rising by 29%. Counterpoint says buyers are postponing upgrades rather than accepting higher prices, following strong iPhone 18 Pro sales in China at launch.

You can now change YouTube’s app icon on your phone, but only if you pay for it

Like other apps, YouTube limits custom icons to Premium subscribers.

•

Nov 26, 2026 — 7:32 AM ET

•

•

Joe Maring / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• YouTube is now letting Premium subscribers change its app icon.

• The current selection includes three options for the icon.

• YouTube has been testing seven app icons in total, but four are missing from the current rollout.

Several prominent apps, including X, Telegram, Reddit, and Instagram, let users swap out the default app icon for something else. Often, this perk is available only to users who pay for the experience. Last month, we learned that YouTube is also working on a similar feature that lets Premium subscribers change the app icon, and it already appears to be rolling out for some folks.

User Radu Oncescu on X posted screenshots of the setting that lets users change the default icon to one of the three other options currently available. These include one with a shiny, metal-like finish, somewhat like a silver YouTube Play button, another one featuring what look like brush strokes using red paint, and a third one with a pixel effect and a gradient over the icon.

X / Radu Oncescu

These options appear under Settings > General > Premium app icon inside the YouTube app. While we spotted the feature being tested on Android, the user notes that it’s available on iOS. Another report from user howfxr on X last week suggests the feature also cropped up for some Android users.

X / howfxr

In both cases, the rollout does not seem to be widespread, and we don’t have it on any of our devices yet. So we recommend not fretting if you don’t have it either yet. It’s not like YouTube is bringing back the original logo with the name spelled out anyway.

Meanwhile, YouTube has been testing four more icon options, including some retro ones, but none appear to be available for now. We’ll keep an eye out for when those might be available.

Black Friday deal: $99 (23% off) until November 30 for Prime members on Amazon.

The Timekettle LiveTalk AI Translation Earbuds work like a real-time interpreter, with a lightweight, open-ear design made for all-day comfort. You can enjoy music, listen to podcasts, and take calls as usual, then switch to translation whenever you need to chat with someone in another language. The comfortable ear-hook design rests outside your ear canal so you can stay aware of your surroundings. And at just 6.9 g each, they’re easy to wear all day.

LiveTalk in the Timekettle app features four handy modes, each designed for a different situation. Face-to-Face Translation helps with two-way conversations, whether each person wears one earbud or one person uses the earbuds while the other speaks through the phone app. And AI Translation Refinement helps make translated sentences sound more natural.

For one-way speech, like lectures, guided tours, or presentations, Live Listening displays a live transcript on your phone and generates real-time AI summaries, helping you quickly review key points as the speaker talks. Voice Call Translation works with both regular and internet calls, while Multimedia Translation makes it easier to follow foreign-language videos, podcasts, and online courses.

LiveTalk supports 54 languages and 108 accents, and it even includes 25 free offline translation packages for flights, remote areas, or when you want to avoid roaming charges.Besides translation, these earbuds are useful for daily use, with customizable EQ settings and the ability to connect to your phone and laptop at the same time. Each charge gives you up to four hours of active translation.

Timekettle is known for its AI translation devices, and LiveTalk is its lighter and more affordable option for everyday use. It’s a good choice for travelers, language learners, multilingual families, or students going abroad next semester.
For Black Friday, Amazon Prime members can get the Timekettle LiveTalk for just $99 (23% off) through November 30.

The Google Pixel 11 Pro XL is a premium Android flagship powered by Tensor G6, with a 6.8-inch 1-120Hz Super Actua display, upgraded triple cameras with 120x Pro Zoom, a 5,115mAh battery, Pixelsnap Qi2.2 charging, and seven years of updates.

Google’s biggest non-folding flagship is $400 off at Amazon, its lowest price yet. The Pixel 11 Pro XL brings Google’s top camera system, a large high-end display and the latest Gemini features. It also gets years of guaranteed updates, which makes it a strong long-term buy at this price.
Narwal Flow 2 Robot Vacuum & Mop — $949.99 ($550 off)
Big suction power and powerful mopping features

The Narwal Flow 2 delivers massive suction power, excellent mops, nearly-perfect hair anti-tangle strategies, and maximum maintenance free operation. AI-powered navigation is reliable, a solid whole-home cleaning experience.

We were already big fans of the Narwal Flow 2 before this superb Black Friday deal came along. It earned an Editor’s Choice award in our review thanks to its excellent cleaning performance, smart navigation, and hands-off convenience. It’s not cheap at its $1,499.99 retail price, but this deal makes it a much more tempting prospect. Narwal’s 2026 flagship has dropped to just $949.99 at both Narwal and Amazon, saving you a hefty $550.

The serious cleaning hardware includes the FlowWash system, which uses a treadmill-style mop, 140-degree water, and 12N of downward pressure to scrub hard floors, while AI DirtSense adjusts the cleaning intensity based on how dirty they are. There’s also 31,000Pa of suction, CarpetFocus technology, and a DualFlow brush system designed to prevent hair tangles.

The smart features are equally impressive. Its NarMind™ Pro system and TwinAI™ Dodge obstacle avoidance use dual RGB cameras and AI to navigate around household clutter, with dedicated Baby Care and Pet Care modes. The dock handles hot-water self-cleaning and hot-air drying, and can automatically empty the dust for up to 120 days. You can get the Flow 2 in Pure White or Black.
The next iteration of the best Sony headphones

The Sony WH-1000XM6 is every bit a worthy successor to Sony's other ANC headphones as you'd hope. They sound very good, have excellent ANC, and are equipped to handle demanding users. However, the lack of cutting-edge connection options might be an issue as the years go by.

Sony’s flagship noise canceling headphones are down to the lowest price Amazon itself has charged. The WH-1000XM6 builds on one of the most popular headphone lines around with stronger noise cancellation, a 12-microphone array for clearer calls, and the return of a foldable design that makes them easier to travel with. Sound quality is rich and detailed out of the box, with plenty of EQ control in Sony’s app, and you get up to 30 hours of playback with noise canceling switched on. All four colors are currently at this price.
Camera-free AI glasses with an invisible heads-up display.

RayNeo iO puts an AI assistant and an invisible heads-up display into frames that look like everyday designer glasses. There's no camera, the frame is IP54 rated, and navigation, live translation and AI answers sit right in your line of sight.
Black Friday deal: $389 (down from $499) until November 30 on Amazon and rayneo.com.

RayNeo iO is the easiest way to put a working AI assistant with an invisible display into your daily life, and this Black Friday it’s $389, down from $499, with a free six-month AI Pro VIP membership included. The glasses look like a stylish pair of everyday designer frames, and the micro-optical heads-up display is invisible to the person sitting across from you.

They’re also completely camera-free. There’s no lens and no recording of any kind, which makes them as easy to wear at dinner or in a meeting as any other pair of glasses — and everyone around you can see that at a glance.

They’re built for daily wear, too. The frame, hinges, and temples are engineered to an IP54 dust and water resistance rating, so a sudden downpour or a dusty trail isn’t something you need to plan around.

Two AI engines come built in, and neither needs a subscription: RayNeo V1 handles instant voice responses, while Google Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite provides contextual reasoning and ambient visual assistance. Those are standard on the glasses and stay yours regardless of what you do about a membership.

The free six-month AI Pro VIP membership then adds hands-free access to frontier models—ChatGPT 5.5, Gemini 3.1 Pro, DeepSeek V4 Pro, Qwen 3.7 Max, and Kimi K2.7—for live translation, deep reasoning, and everyday productivity. It applies to any iO bought between November 19 and November 30, and unlocks automatically when you activate the glasses by December 18, 2026.

Navigation is the feature you’ll reach for most. Directional arrows, street names, and live transit alerts sit in your natural line of sight, so your phone stays in your pocket wherever you walk or cycle.

There’s an extra reason to watch the second half of the sale if you wear prescription lenses. From November 27 to 30, base custom lenses are free on prescription-ready configurations — a $159 value — which means a prescription-equipped iO costs the same $389 as the standard pair, and upgraded lenses are free for the first 100 orders worldwide. If you want the dedicated portable charging case, the bundle is $428, down from $549.

And they keep getting better. RayNeo ships regular over-the-air updates, and the RayNeo iO SDK goes public in December 2026 — built so that people with no programming experience can create, upload, and share apps for the glasses. You describe what you want and build it by asking, which opens the door to unprecedented software: a recipe app that holds the next step in your eyeline while your hands are covered in flour, a reader that keeps your book above the handlebars, a custom tutorial for a specific hands-free task, a pace display for your morning run. You’ll also be able to wire up your own AI assistants and connect to third-party Bluetooth devices.

That’s the real case for buying in at $389 on Amazon or rayneo.com. The hardware is ready today — stylish, camera-free, and built to be worn in any weather — and the software is about to be handed to anyone with an idea and a sentence to describe it. These are glasses that become more valuable with every week you own them.
Black Friday deal: $999 at Best Buy (save $100).

Googlebooks are barely out of the gate, but our readers have already picked a favorite. Lenovo’s Googlebook 15 came out on top in our recent poll of the five launch models, and its hardware goes some way toward explaining why. Better still, Best Buy has knocked $100 off the price for Black Friday, bringing this Android-based laptop down to $999.

Lenovo’s pitch is “Built to move at the speed of you. Simplify your day with Lenovo Googlebook 15 powered by Intel® Core™ Ultra 5 Series 3 processor.” That chip is paired with 16GB of RAM and 512GB of storage, but the big attraction might be the screen. You get a 15.3-inch 3K OLED touchscreen with a smooth 120Hz refresh rate, plus four Dolby Atmos speakers. That makes it a great option for watching a movie once you’re done being productive. And despite the large display, the laptop weighs less than three pounds.

Naturally, much of the excitement around Googlebooks is about the software. Gemini features include Magic Pointer, which can help you add calendar dates from whatever you’re looking at onscreen, and Rambler, which tidies up dictated thoughts. You can also access compatible apps and files from your Android phone, potentially saving you plenty of back-and-forth between devices.

There are a few other Best Buy perks worth knowing about. You can check whether your old laptop qualifies for trade-in, while selected accessories and networking products are available at 25% off with eligible purchases. Best Buy also includes six months of Webroot security software and a full year of Google AI Pro at no extra cost.

The Phone 3 is a stylish reinvention of Nothing's Android phone series, now with flagship specs, including a large silicon-carbon battery, a Qualcomm Snapdragon 8s Gen 4 chipset, and a periscope zoom lens with macro photography support.

Nothing’s flagship phone is back down to its lowest price, knocking $200 off the 256GB model. The Phone (3) stands out for its transparent design and the Glyph Matrix display on the back, which can show notifications, timers, and more without waking the screen. It’s no style-over-substance device, though: you get a Snapdragon 8s Gen 4 chip, a bright AMOLED display, four 50MP cameras, and a 5,150mAh battery, all running Nothing’s clean and thoughtful take on Android. Need more space? The 512GB model is also $200 off at $599.

Handhelds are great for gaming on the go, but that little screen isn’t ideal when you want to play with friends. The Aurzen ZIP Pro offers a handy alternative, letting you project your games onto a much bigger surface without needing a TV. Its compact tri-fold body fits in a jacket pocket, yet delivers native 1080p projection. It connects directly to a Nintendo Switch over USB-C, with a dedicated Game Mode offering 20-40ms latency.

It’s also useful beyond gaming and movie nights. For example, sewing enthusiasts can project digital patterns onto a worktable instead of printing and taping together pages. The standard ZIP Pro is down to $579.99 (regularly $629.99) through November 30. Early buyers can also score a free GoPlay Portable Carrying Case or Z-Stand.

For more conventional viewing, the built-in battery offers up to 2.5 hours in ECO Mode, and two people can listen privately using Bluetooth headphones.

There’s also a more eye-catching option for art lovers. Aurzen is also running a sitewide Black Friday draw through November 30, giving customers who order a chance to get their purchase for free. The results and winners will be announced on Aurzen’s official Instagram and Facebook accounts.

blocks.text: Waterdrop M6CG Hot & Cold Countertop RO System

The Waterdrop M6CG Countertop RO System is an installation-free water purifier with 8-stage reverse-osmosis filtration, remineralization, and instant hot and cold water. It offers adjustable temperatures, a detachable glass pitcher, and a 3:1 pure-to-drain ratio.
Black Friday deal: $388.55 on Amazon with code AA26BFCM (save $150.45).

A water filter might not be top of your tech wishlist, but the Waterdrop M6CG certainly impressed our own Edgar Cervantes. After spending a few weeks testing it, he liked it so much that he moved it next to his desk and declared that it had genuinely improved his daily life — hence the Android Authority recommendation. Better still, Black Friday has brought the M6CG down to $409 from $539 on Amazon. Use our exclusive code AA26BFCM at checkout from November 19 through November 30 to bring it down to $388.55.

blocks.alt: Waterdrop M6CG Hot & Cold Reverse Osmosis System

blocks.text: The M6CG is a 2026 countertop reverse osmosis system, meaning no plumbing work or permanent installation is required. That’s a big plus if you’re renting, short on kitchen space, or want something for an office or RV. Its eight-stage filtration system removes impurities from tap water before adding minerals back to improve the taste.

More unusually, it handles both hot and cold water, with temperatures ranging from 59 to 203 degrees. That means the same machine can provide chilled water for a refreshing drink or piping-hot water for your morning coffee. Five dispensing volumes and a customizable Favorite Mode let you save your preferred temperature and quantity, while the detachable 40 oz glass pitcher is handy for serving guests, cooking, or keeping water in the fridge.

Separate tap-water and wastewater compartments prevent the two from mixing, while its efficient 3:1 pure-to-drain ratio means three parts filtered water for every part discarded. You can even reuse the wastewater for household cleaning or watering suitable plants. It’s a premium purchase, but the convenience of having mineral-enriched hot and cold water on demand makes it an attractive option.
Powerful flagship with top-tier cameras, AI, and privacy features.

The Galaxy S26 Ultra is Samsung's slimmest and lightest Ultra yet, pairing a 6.9-inch display with the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy and a redesigned cooling system. It doubles down on imaging with a brighter 200MP main camera, upgraded zoom, advanced 8K video features, and Ultra-exclusive privacy and Galaxy AI tools.

Samsung’s top-tier flagship is $350 off at Amazon, and the deal applies to every color. The Galaxy S26 Ultra pairs a huge 6.9-inch display with Samsung’s new Privacy Display, a 200MP main camera, and Super Fast Charging 3.0, making it one of the most complete Android phones you can buy.
Vocci Ring for up to 35% off, plus three months of Vocci Pro
Black Friday deal: Save up to 35%, with three months of Vocci Pro included, from November 26 to 30 at Vocci.

The Vocci Ring is a wearable AI note-taker. It records your meetings so you can focus on the conversation and remember what was agreed. It’s made of titanium and weighs just a few grams, so it’s comfortable to wear all day.

To start recording, simply double-click the ring — there’s no need to take out your phone. A single click lets you mark an important moment, like a deadline or an important number. You’ll get a quick confirmation with a small light and a gentle vibration. The ring records for up to eight hours on a single charge, and the charging case can recharge it about three times.

Once everything is synced, you can open the Vocci app to view the transcript, summary, and to-dos. So, if a client asks you to revise the budget and timeline in their proposal, you can revisit the meeting notes to see exactly what they requested. Then, you can use Vocci AI to draft a response and, of course, make any edits you’d like before sending it.

And with Vocci Desktop, you can easily add notes to your online meetings. Your calls and synced Ring sessions are all saved in the same Vocci account, so you can find everything in one convenient place.

The Vocci Ring is a great fit for anyone with a busy schedule of client meetings, sales calls, and team check-ins. It’s available in two finishes, usually priced at $249 and $299. From November 26 to November 30, you can get $30 off each model during Vocci’s Black Friday sale, bringing the price down to $219 or $269. Every purchase during the sale also includes three free months of Vocci Pro.
Get up to 35% off and three months of Vocci Pro through November 30.

The Google Pixel Watch 5 is a premium smartwatch with a brighter 3,000-nit AMOLED display, Snapdragon W5 Gen 2 processor, and advanced Gemini-powered assistance, alongside improved GPS, breathing emergency detection, blood pressure trend monitoring, and up to 40 hours of battery life in the 45mm model.

Google’s newest smartwatch is already $100 cheaper than its launch price, matching the lowest price we’ve seen on Amazon. The 41mm Pixel Watch 5 keeps the familiar domed design but adds a brighter display that reaches 3,000 nits, double the storage, and a faster chip than last year’s model. Battery life stretches to around 30 hours with the always-on display enabled, and you get Google’s full suite of health, sleep, and workout tracking built in. This price applies to the Obsidian Wi-Fi model.
Excellent image quality and a plethora of safety features

The Botslab Dash Cam G980H offers premium features with a Sony IMX 415 sensor recording in 4K and a 170-degree front view, plus a 1080p rear camera with a 150-degree view. It excels in low light with an f/1.5 aperture. Safety alerts, GPS tracking, and even parking mode round up a great product.
Black Friday deal: $180.49 (33% off, saving $89.50) with code BOTSLABBF until December 31 on Amazon.

The Botslab G980H 4-Channel dashcam records the road ahead, traffic behind, and both sides of your car, all at the same time. This gives you peace of mind on the road and provides clear footage for your insurer or the police if they need to understand how an accident happened. It can be especially helpful in heavy traffic, on multi-lane roads, and in busy parking lots.

The front camera records in 3K, while three 1080p cameras cover the rear and both sides. The two side cameras attach magnetically, so you can set them up and remove them quickly. You can use all four cameras, switch to three, or keep things simple with just the front and rear cameras. In the supported 3- and 2-channel modes, the front camera can also record in 4K for a little extra detail on the road ahead.

You’re covered even after you park. Pairing it with a compatible hardwire kit (sold separately) adds three helpful parking features. Sentry Mode starts recording when it detects motion around your vehicle, while collision detection captures footage if your car is hit. And with time-lapse recording, it condenses hours of parked time into a short video that’s easy to review.

The main unit features a 3.18″ touchscreen that makes setup and playback easy. Recordings appear in a convenient four-way split screen, letting you compare feeds from all the cameras at once. You can also take a photo or start recording with a voice command, while keeping both hands on the wheel.

Built-in GPS records your driving alongside your footage. You can download videos over the 5.8GHz Wi-Fi connection through the Botslab app, and a 128GB memory card is included, so you’ll have plenty of storage from the start.

The G980H 4-channel dashcam is a great choice if you’d like a comprehensive view around your car, with the flexibility to use just a couple of cameras if you don’t need all four. It’s also a great gift for someone who drives a lot for work, often parks on the street, or has a long holiday road trip coming up.
Bright new face, same reliable activity tracking.

The brand-new Garmin Instinct 3 might not be it's most expensive GPS watch, but it shows impressive value with new creature comforts like a built-in flashlight, updated satellite features, and a can't-miss AMOLED face in either a 45mm or 50mm case.

Garmin’s Instinct 3 AMOLED has dropped to its lowest price ever, a full $100 below what it sold for through most of the fall. It brings a bright AMOLED screen to Garmin’s rugged Instinct line, alongside multi-band GPS, a built-in LED flashlight, and the detailed health and training tracking Garmin is known for. The deal applies to the 45mm model in Black.

You can cover your home with three of Blink’s newest outdoor cameras for less than the usual price of one, thanks to this record-low deal that slashes 66% off. Each Blink Outdoor 2K+ records sharp 2K video with improved audio and night vision, and a pair of AA lithium batteries lasts up to two years, so there’s no wiring to worry about. The Sync Module Core is included in the box, and you can check feeds and get motion alerts from the Blink app or an Alexa device. It’s an easy way to build out a full security setup on a tight budget.
Buy travel data before you fly and be online as soon as you land, with no roaming charges.

Yesim is a Swiss travel eSIM provider with country, regional, and global plans, from small data bundles to unlimited data. One eSIM on your phone lets you switch plans as you move between countries, which is handy on multi-stop trips.
Black Friday deal: 20% off select plans (Nov 20–29) on yesim.app

Sorting out your mobile data before you travel is an easy way to save money. With a travel eSIM, you can purchase data for your destination ahead of time, so you’re online as soon as you arrive and can avoid roaming charges on your regular plan. Yesim is a Swiss company founded in 2019 and is one of the first in the travel eSIM space. Today, it has more than 4 million users and coverage in over 200 destinations.

Yesim has country, regional, and global plans, and everything from small data bundles to unlimited data. You can have one travel eSIM on your phone and switch plans as you go from country to country, which is very useful on multi-stop trips. To get started, make sure your phone is compatible (iPhone XS or later, and most recent Android phones).
Then download the Yesim app to manage your plan, but during Black Friday, buy on yesim.app, as the promo codes only work on the website.

Both new and existing customers can participate, so it’s worth checking back a few times over the course of the week.

If you buy a featured plan with the promo code, you’re also entered into a prize draw. The draw takes place after the promotion has finished. Prizes include GetYourGuide gift cards or promo codes, flight vouchers, and Amazon gift cards, so your savings on data could go toward an excursion or a flight.

Plans purchased during the sale can be activated up to 180 days later. So you can buy now for a Christmas trip, a winter break, or even travel next spring. Outside of the sale, new users can get 15% off with the code GETYESIM15.
Amazon’s first color Kindle with stylus support
Amazon’s Kindle Scribe Colorsoft brings color to E-Ink, offering a thinner design, improved lighting, and smarter pen tools for its most advanced reading and writing experience yet.

Amazon’s first color Kindle with pen support is down to its lowest price ever, $30 below what it hit on Prime Day. items.body: Apple could offer a limited-edition iPhone 20 Pro model that incorporates ceramic, according to the Chinese leaker known as Fixed Focus Digital. In a post on Weibo , the leaker claimed to have gotten their hands on ceramic components for the 20th-anniversary iPhone, which is expected to launch next year. The leaker said that production capacity for the components is planned to be very low, suggesting they will be for a limited-edition model. In a follow-up comment, the leaker claimed that the project would enter mass production if it passes engineering validation testing (EVT), and even joked that its scarcity could make it appreciate in value. The leaker doesn't say what kind of ceramic components they have in their possession, leaving it unclear whether Apple is considering a ceramic rear panel, a larger section of the enclosure, or a smaller exterior part. Apple already offers ceramic as a premium casing material on the Apple Watch Series 12, which comes in Pearl White and Night Blue ceramic alongside aluminum and titanium options. The company also previously sold ceramic Apple Watch Edition models, including a white ceramic version of the Series 5. Interestingly, the ‌iPhone Air‌ features Ceramic Shield 2 on the front and Ceramic Shield on the back, and Fixed Focus Digital has previously said next year's iPhone 20 Pro models will use the same glass design , but with more pronounced curves along all four sides of a titanium frame. Ceramic Shield incorporates tiny ceramic crystals within a glass matrix, which preserves transparency while improving durability. However, the wording of the leaker's latest post suggests that ceramic could be applied in a more visually prominent way. Apple's 20th-anniversary iPhone models are expected to launch in the fall of 2027 with a radical glass-centric redesign featuring a quad-curved display . Google is working on gamepad profiles for Android’s controller remapping feature

You might not have to remap your controller every time you launch a different game.

•

Nov 26, 2026 — 7:12 AM ET

•

•

Joe Maring / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• Google is working on adding support for multiple gamepad profiles in Android.

• Code in Android 17 QPR3 Beta 4 hints at a new interface for managing gamepad profiles.

• The feature could let users switch between gamepad button layouts on the fly.

If you’re a mobile gamer, you probably use controllers for many Android games. Customizing a controller’s layout can be quite useful, especially if you like using different layouts for different games. Although Google added support for game controller remapping with Android 17, it currently lets you keep only one layout saved at a time. Fortunately, Google is now working to improve the feature with support for multiple gamepad profiles.

APK teardown

This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship.

You're reading an Android Authority exclusive story you won’t find anywhere else. An APK teardown helps predict features that may arrive on a service in the future based on work-in-progress code. However, it is possible that such predicted features may not make it to a public release. More Authority Insights →

While digging through the code in Android 17 QPR3 Beta 4, we spotted several strings that point to an upcoming gamepad profile management interface. According to the strings, there could be a “Default” profile, along with options to edit and delete individual profiles. We also spotted strings hinting at a “More options” menu for each profile.

Here are the strings we found related to the feature:

Code

<string name="gamepad_profile_default_title">Default</string>
<string name="gamepad_profile_menu_delete">Delete</string>
<string name="gamepad_profile_menu_edit">Edit</string>
<string name="gamepad_profile_more_options_content_description">More options for %1$s</string>

We also gathered some details on how the feature will work by taking a closer look at the code. Android will distinguish between “default” and “global” profiles, and it seems the global profiles will be reusable across controllers. We also spotted functionality to retrieve saved profiles, switch between them, and identify the active profile. Android could also let users edit the default profile, but won’t let them delete it.

Here are the references we spotted in the code:

Code

default_profile
global_profile_
getGamepadProfileHeaders
getAppliedGamepadProfiles
applyGamepadProfile
deleteGamepadProfile
launchEditProfileFragment

Letting gamers create multiple gamepad profiles could let them set up custom button layouts for different game styles. Instead of manually remapping buttons every time, the feature could let you simply switch between saved profiles.

The feature isn’t live yet, and we couldn’t get it to show up on our test device. However, since we’re already seeing the groundwork for a dedicated gamepad layout interface, it seems Google is making progress on the feature.
